questions.question: Which of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India added a new fundamental duty under Article 51-A?
questions.solution:
The Eighty-Sixth Amendment Act, 2002 added the 11th Fundamental Duty to Article 51-A.
  • The Duty: It mandates that a parent or guardian provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of 6 and 14 years.
  • Significance: This amendment also inserted Article 21A (Right to Education) and changed the subject matter of Article 45.

questions.question: In which year was the ‘Lotteries Regulation Act’ passed?
questions.solution:
The Lotteries Regulation Act was passed in 1998.
  • Purpose: It was enacted to regulate lotteries and provide for matters connected therewith, allowing State governments to prohibit the sale of lottery tickets within their jurisdiction.
  • Control: Under this act, a lottery cannot be organized, conducted, or promoted except by the State Government.

questions.question: The Election Commission of India (ECI) is the watchdog of free and fair elections in the country and ______ of the Constitution of India provides for its establishment.
questions.solution:
Article 324 of the Constitution provides for the establishment, powers, and functions of the Election Commission of India (ECI).
  • Role: It acts as the watchdog to ensure free and fair elections to the Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of the President and Vice-President.
  • Structure: Currently, it consists of a Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners.

questions.question: As per the Hindu Succession Act 1956, who amongst the following has the first right over the property of a Hindu woman who dies intestate?
questions.option_2: The legal heirs of her father
questions.option_4: The legal heirs of her husband
questions.solution:
Under the Hindu Succession Act 1956, if a Hindu woman dies intestate (without a will), her husband (and her children) has the first right over her property.
  • Order of Succession: The property devolves first upon the sons, daughters, and the husband.
  • Secondary Heirs: In their absence, the property goes to the heirs of the husband, then to the parents, and finally to the heirs of the father and mother.

questions.question: With reference to the Constituent Assembly, which of the following statements is correct?
questions.option_1: The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Flag in July 1949.
questions.option_2: The Constituent Assembly ratified India's membership of the Commonwealth in May 1947.
questions.option_3: The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Anthem in January 1950.
questions.option_4: The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Song in January 1948.
questions.solution:
The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Anthem ('Jana Gana Mana') on January 24, 1950.
  • National Flag: It was actually adopted on July 22, 1947.
  • Commonwealth: India's membership was ratified in May 1949.
  • National Song: 'Vande Mataram' was also adopted as the National Song on January 24, 1950.

questions.question: How many female members were part of the Constituent Assembly that framed the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
There were 15 female members in the Constituent Assembly that framed the Constitution of India.
  • Prominent Members: These included Sarojini Naidu, Vijayalakshmi Pandit, Rajkumari Amrit Kaur, and Sucheta Kripalani.
  • Note: Their contribution was vital in ensuring gender equality provisions within the Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act 2009 is an Act of Parliament which came into force in:
questions.solution:
The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act 2009 (RTE Act) officially came into force on April 1, 2010.
  • Legal Status: It gives legal shape to the Fundamental Right promised under Article 21A.
  • Scope: India became one of the few countries in the world to make education a justiciable right.

questions.question: The idea of having a provision for a Bicameral Parliament in the Constitution of India was borrowed from the ______ Constitution.
questions.solution:
The provision for a Bicameral Parliament (two houses: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) was borrowed from the British Constitution.
  • Other Borrowings: India also adopted the Parliamentary form of government, the rule of law, and single citizenship from the UK.
  • Definition: Bicameralism refers to a legislative body with two distinct chambers.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India declared that the Parliament has the power to abridge or take away any of the Fundamental Rights under Article 368 and such an Act, will NOT be a law under the meaning of Article 13?
questions.solution:
The Twenty-fourth Amendment Act, 1971 affirmed that Parliament has the power to abridge any Fundamental Right using Article 368.
  • Article 13: It clarified that constitutional amendments are not considered 'laws' under Article 13, thereby shielding them from judicial review based on Fundamental Rights violations at that time.
  • Context: This was a reaction to the Supreme Court's judgment in the Golaknath case.

questions.question: The Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (Amendment) Bill, 2021, which was passed in March 2021 amended the Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi Act, ______.
questions.solution:
The Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (Amendment) Bill, 2021 amended the original GNCTD Act of 1991.
  • Key Change: It defined the term 'Government' in the context of laws made by the Delhi Legislative Assembly to mean the Lieutenant Governor (LG).
  • Impact: It increased the discretionary powers of the LG over the elected government of Delhi.

questions.question: Who among the following presidents of India gave assent to the 100th Amendment of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
President Pranab Mukherjee gave his assent to the 100th Amendment Act, 2015.
  • Subject: This amendment ratified the Land Boundary Agreement (LBA) between India and Bangladesh.
  • Outcome: It involved the exchange of enclaves and the transfer of adverse possessions between the two nations.

questions.question: In which of the following years was an Act to provide for the reorganisation of the states of India and for matters connected therewith enacted?
questions.solution:
The States Reorganisation Act was enacted in 1956.
  • Basis: It reorganized state boundaries along linguistic lines.
  • Structure: It resulted in the creation of 14 states and 6 union territories.
  • Amendment: This was facilitated by the 7th Constitutional Amendment.

questions.question: An amendment to the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 was passed in the year ______.
questions.solution:
A landmark amendment to the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 was passed in the year 2005.
  • Daughter's Rights: It gave daughters equal rights in ancestral property (coparcenary rights) as sons.
  • Gender Justice: It removed the gender discriminatory provisions regarding property inheritance.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India gave the status of state to Goa?
questions.solution:
The 56th Amendment Act, 1987 conferred the status of a state to Goa.
  • Union Territory: Prior to this, Goa was part of the Union Territory of Goa, Daman, and Diu.
  • Result: Goa became the 25th state of India, while Daman and Diu remained a Union Territory.

questions.question: The greater one-horned rhino is listed under the Schedule ______ of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.
questions.solution:
The Greater One-Horned Rhino is listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.
  • Protection Level: Schedule I provides the highest level of legal protection in India.
  • Offenses: Hunting or trade of animals listed in this schedule attracts the harshest penalties.

questions.question: The Contempt of Courts Act was passed to define and limit the powers of certain courts in punishing contempt of courts and to regulate their procedure in relation thereto. In which of the following years was the Act passed?
questions.solution:
The Contempt of Courts Act was passed in 1971.
  • Definition: It defines Civil Contempt (willful disobedience of court orders) and Criminal Contempt (scandalizing the court).
  • Objective: To maintain the dignity and authority of the courts while regulating the power to punish for contempt.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Dowry Prohibition Act passed in India?
questions.solution:
The Dowry Prohibition Act was passed in 1961.
  • Prohibition: It prohibits the giving or taking of dowry in India.
  • Joint Session: Notably, this act was passed in a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament due to a deadlock.

questions.question: The ______ Constitutional Amendment Act gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions.
questions.solution:
The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions.
  • New Part: It added Part IX to the Constitution titled 'The Panchayats'.
  • Schedule: It also added the Eleventh Schedule containing 29 functional items for Panchayats.

questions.question: Which of the following Indian Acts was passed in the year 2005?
questions.option_2: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act
questions.solution:
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act was passed in 2005.
  • Objective: To provide more effective protection for the rights of women who are victims of violence of any kind occurring within the family.
  • Definition: It defines domestic violence broadly to include physical, sexual, verbal, emotional, and economic abuse.

questions.question: The ______ Amendment of the Constitution of India envisages the Gram Sabha as the foundation of the Panchayat Raj System to perform functions and powers entrusted to it by the State Legislatures.
questions.solution:
The 73rd Amendment establishes the Gram Sabha as the foundation of the Panchayat Raj System.
  • Definition: A Gram Sabha consists of all persons registered in the electoral rolls of a village within the Panchayat area.
  • Powers: It exercises powers and performs functions at the village level as determined by the State Legislature.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendments to the Constitution of India was passed with the primary objective to constitutionally encode the re-organisation of Indian States based on language?
questions.solution:
The Seventh Amendment Act, 1956 was passed to constitutionally implement the reorganization of states based on language.
  • Changes: It abolished the existing classification of states (Part A, B, C, and D) and introduced the State and Union Territory structure.
  • Article 1: It amended Article 1 and the First Schedule of the Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following legislations ought to allow senior Indian magistrates to preside over cases involving British subjects in India?
questions.solution:
The Ilbert Bill, 1884 was a controversial piece of legislation that sought to allow Indian magistrates to try British subjects in criminal cases.
  • White Mutiny: It faced severe opposition from the British community in India, leading to a 'White Mutiny'.
  • Compromise: The bill was ultimately amended to require a jury, of which at least half were Europeans, for such trials.

questions.question: The 60th Amendment to the Constitution of India increased the ceiling of profession tax from ₹ 250 p.a. to ______ p.a.
questions.solution:
The 60th Amendment Act, 1988 increased the ceiling of profession tax from ₹250 per annum to ₹2,500 per annum.
  • Article 276: This amendment modified Article 276(2) of the Constitution.
  • Benefit: It allowed State Governments to raise more revenue through taxes on professions, trades, callings, and employments.

questions.question: Which amendment to the Constitution of India changed the description of India from a ‘sovereign democratic republic’ to a ‘sovereign, socialist secular democratic republic’ and also changed the words ‘unity of the nation’ to ‘unity and integrity of the nation’?
questions.solution:
The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 (often called the 'Mini-Constitution') added the words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' to the Preamble.
  • Integrity: It also changed 'unity of the nation' to 'unity and integrity of the nation'.
  • Era: This was passed during the National Emergency under the Indira Gandhi government.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Citizenship Act passed for the first time in India?
questions.solution:
The Citizenship Act was passed for the first time in India in 1955.
  • Acquisition: It provides for the acquisition of citizenship by birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and incorporation of territory.
  • Constitution: While Articles 5-11 of the Constitution deal with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution, the 1955 Act regulates it thereafter.

questions.question: A bill becomes an Act of the Parliament after being passed by both the houses of Parliament and assented to by the ______.
questions.solution:
A bill becomes an Act only after receiving the assent of the President.
  • Process: After being passed by the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, the bill is sent to the President under Article 111.
  • Options: The President can give assent, withhold assent, or return the bill (if not a Money Bill) for reconsideration.

questions.question: Article ______ of the Constitution of India lays down the process for introducing changes in the Constitution.
questions.solution:
Article 368 details the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and the procedure for doing so.
  • Initiation: An amendment can be initiated only by the introduction of a Bill in either House of Parliament.
  • Strict Rule: There is no provision for a joint sitting of the two houses for passing a Constitutional Amendment Bill.

questions.question: With reference to the Money Bills in the Parliament, which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
questions.option_1: It can be rejected or amended by the Rajya Sabha.
questions.option_2: It can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha.
questions.option_3: The Lok Sabha can either accept or reject all or any of the recommendations of the Rajya Sabha.
questions.option_4: It can only be introduced by a minister and not by a private member.
questions.solution:
The statement that a Money Bill 'can be rejected or amended by the Rajya Sabha' is INCORRECT.
  • Reality: The Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend a Money Bill; it can only make recommendations.
  • Deadline: If the bill is not returned within 14 days, it is deemed to have been passed by both Houses in the form it was passed by the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act or Right to Education (RTE) Act is an Act of the Parliament of India enacted in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The Right to Education (RTE) Act was enacted by Parliament in 2009.
  • Full Name: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009.
  • Constitutional Link: It was enacted to give effect to Article 21A, which makes education a fundamental right for children aged 6-14.

questions.question: Who was the chairman of the House Committee of the Constituent Assembly of India?
questions.solution:
B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya was the chairman of the House Committee of the Constituent Assembly.
  • Role: The committee dealt with the residential accommodation and other facilities for the members of the Assembly.
  • Note: He was also a prominent leader and historian of the Indian National Congress.
